tagline.text: A beginner-friendly Sierra Madre ridge trek in Rodriguez, doable as a day trip from Manila

location.label: Location
location.text: Sitio Balagbag, Barangay San Isidro, Rodriguez, Rizal

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,200 (day trip from Manila, per person)

children.text: Mt. Balagbag rises about 777–787 m above sea level in the Sierra Madre foothills of Rodriguez (formerly Montalban), Rizal. It takes about 2–3 hours from Manila by public transport, and from the summit you can see the Metro Manila skyline and the sunrise, which makes it a popular first hike.
Mt. Balagbag stands in Barangay San Isidro, Rodriguez, Rizal, at the western edge of the Sierra Madre range. Its height is given as anywhere from about
to

depending on the source, so think of it as a bit taller than a neighborhood hill. Hiking communities rate it 3 out of 9 in difficulty with a trail class of 1–2, which puts it in the beginner category.
Its popularity comes from easy access. From Cubao in Quezon City you take a bus to Tungko, then a jeepney to Licao-Licao, and the climb from the jump-off to the summit usually takes about
1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours

. The trail is wide and fairly gentle, so many mountain bikers and trail runners come here too. The area is also said to have been used to film the Battle of Tirad Pass scenes in the movie Goyo: Ang Batang Heneral. On weekends and holidays the registration area can get crowded, so a weekday or an early start is more relaxed.

From the top you can see the Sierra Madre ridgeline, the plains of Bulacan and Laguna, and on clear days the high-rises of Metro Manila. However, the ridge is open ground with almost no tree shade, so the sun is strong by day, and most people start before dawn and come down early in the morning. Some people camp to see the sunrise, a sea of clouds, and the city lights at night. For first-timers, the flow is as follows: bus from Cubao to Tungko, jeepney from Tungko to Licao-Licao, then a tricycle or a walk to the barangay registration post. There you write your name, pay the registration fee, head to the jump-off and climb to the summit. The transfers can take longer than the hike itself, so plan on half a day to a full day round trip from Manila.

Many of the fees and rules in this guide come from blogs and reviews written between 2018 and 2022. Registration fees and whether a guide is mandatory differ from source to source, so check with the barangay help desk or recent reviews before you go.

From the summit the Sierra Madre ridgeline and the plains toward Bulacan and Laguna spread out, and in good weather the high-rises of Ortigas and Makati show up as tiny shapes. Early morning, when the air is clearest, gives the sharpest view.
If you camp or climb very early, you can watch the sun rise over the eastern ridge. A sea of clouds appears on some days and not others depending on season and weather, so do not count on it.

Most of the trail is wide and gentle, so even first-time hikers feel little pressure. Some sections have large rocks, loose stones and steep slopes, so wear hiking shoes or sandals with firm soles. After the paved and sandy start the path turns to dirt, and views open up along the ridge, which makes good rest spots.

blocks.title: A distance that suits a day hike

children.text: The full trail is known to be about
7 km
, and the summit takes 1.5–2 hours. If you leave Manila at dawn you can be down before lunch and plan the afternoon. Even if you do not camp, bring a packed lunch and snacks to enjoy at the top.

Many people camp overnight near the summit and at the mid-trail campsite. At night you can see distant city lights, and on clear nights stars too. Tents are not rented at the jump-off, so bring your own. The campsite is a windy ridge, so pack tent stakes and a windbreaker.

The wide ridge trail also draws mountain bikers and trail runners. Because they share the path with hikers, everyone should yield to each other. When riding or running in a group, slow down and signal to people ahead with a bell or your voice.
The area is said to have been used to film the Battle of Tirad Pass scenes in the movie Goyo: Ang Batang Heneral. If you have seen the film, the ridge scenery may look familiar.

items.title: Day hike
items.subtitle: Leave at dawn and be down before lunch

children.text: Meet around the Cubao bus terminal. The earlier the Tungko bus leaves, the more you avoid the sun.
Get off in front of the BDO in Tungko (San Jose del Monte, Bulacan) and walk to the jeepney terminal. Jeepneys to Licao-Licao leave only when full, so hurry.
From Licao-Licao take a tricycle or walk to the barangay registration post. Write your name and group size, pay the registration fee, and check then whether you need a guide.
Start the hike at the Sitio Balagbag jump-off. The start is paved and sandy road, and further on you reach dirt trail and large rocks.
Reach the summit, enjoy the view and take photos. There is almost no shade, so you need a hat, sunscreen and water.
Start descending. Many reviews say the descent is trickier than the climb because of loose stones, so take your time.
Use the restroom and freshen up near the registration post, then take a jeepney to Tungko and a bus back to Cubao.

Times to the summit range from 1.5 to 2.5 hours depending on the review, so leave room in your plan if it is your first time. If you cannot manage a dawn start, starting after 8:00 a.m. is not recommended because of the midday heat.
Meet at Cubao or Tungko, travel to Licao-Licao and finish registration.
Climb slowly with your pack. You must bring water, cooking gear and a tent yourself.
Choose a campsite and pitch your tent. It is best to finish preparing dinner before dark.
Turn in for the night. Keep your belongings inside the tent and do not bring valuables.
Watch the sunrise and have breakfast.
Break camp, pack out all trash and descend. Plan to reach Manila late in the afternoon to be safe.
Some reviews mention an extra camping fee (about ₱30). Theft incidents have been reported, so go with a group of 4–9 people.

The road is narrow with many motorcycles and jeepneys, so go early in the morning.

The dry season from November to May is the best time to hike. December to February is relatively cool.
March to May is clear but with almost no shade, so daytime hiking is hard. An early start is a must.
In the rainy season (June–November) the trail is slippery and foggy on many days. Check the weather forecast before you leave.

items.label: Registration fee
items.note: 2018-2022 reviews: environmental/logbook fee ₱10-20, holiday or day registration ₱50-60, ₱25 also reported, so confirm on site

items.label: Guide
items.note: Optional or required (reviews disagree), ₱300-500 reported for a group of 5-7 (2011-2022 reviews), confirm on site

items.label: Bus to Tungko (from Cubao)
items.note: Varies with air-conditioned or ordinary bus, ₱50-70 in 2012-2022 reviews

items.label: Tricycle
items.note: Licao-Licao to the jump-off, one way per person (2018-2022 reviews), ₱60-70 reported to the farthest point

items.note: Available at shops near the jump-off

There is almost no lodging in the village at the foot of the mountain, so most people do a day trip or camp. Tents are not rented. To stay overnight it is easier to book a room in Manila or around Tungko. Tungko is a transport hub where buses to Cubao and jeepneys part ways, so a same-day round trip is easy as long as you catch the last ride.

Near the registration post and along the trail, small neighborhood stores (sari-sari stores) sell drinks and snacks, and reviews mention a stall selling halo-halo and ice cream. There are no shops at the summit, so bring your own meal, snacks and water.

A common routine is to sleep early in Manila the night before and have a simple breakfast at a restaurant or convenience store near the Tungko terminal. Since midday hiking is hard, a realistic plan is to return to Tungko or Cubao after the descent and eat lunch there. Whether local eateries are open varies by day, so check on site.
Bring at least about
2 liters
of water per person. The mountain is said to have no natural drinking water source.
With little shade, prepare a hat, sunscreen and a thin long-sleeved shirt.
Hiking shoes or sandals with firm soles are safest. It is easy to slip on the descent, where loose stones are common.
Jeepneys to Licao-Licao leave only when full, so get to Tungko early at dawn.
Whether a local guide is mandatory and the registration fee change over time, so check recent reviews and barangay notices. These may differ from earlier reviews.
Carry out all trash and do not pick roadside plants.
Mobile signal is said to be generally available, but a power bank gives peace of mind.
Avoid rainy days when the trail turns muddy, and check the forecast before you leave.
The view from the summit is clearest early in the morning. After 9:00 a.m. haze or clouds often roll in, so aim to arrive around 7–8 a.m.
Hiring a guide reduces the chance of getting lost and helps the local community. Ask at the registration post about the exact cost.
Theft incidents were reported in 2014 and 2017, so avoid hiking or camping alone and leave valuables at home.
On the open ridge, heatstroke and dehydration are serious risks in the daytime. Avoid climbing in the midday sun.
The descent has loose stones and soil, so falls are easy.
In the rainy season the mud makes the trail confusing and slippery.
Check permits and rules for camping with the barangay before you camp.
Many stretches are said to have mobile signal, but some may be weak, so prepare an offline map and your group's contact numbers in advance.
There are almost no trash bins, so take all your trash back and dispose of it in the city.
A conservation area in Baras, Rizal, and another place to visit in the same province. By car it takes
about 1 to 2 hours or more
, so plan a separate day for it.
Another hiking and cave destination in eastern Rizal. It is far, so combining it on the same day is difficult.
A park in San Miguel, Bulacan, relatively close, but confirm the travel time on site.
